nodes.label: GraphX
nodes.rationale: GraphX builds a persistent knowledge graph from code, documentation, papers, images, and videos, enabling query-based navigation instead of grepping through files. Relationships survive across sessions and are tagged EXTRACTED, INFERRED, or AMBIGUOUS.

nodes.label: graphify
nodes.rationale: graphify is a Claude Code skill backed by a Python library. The skill orchestrates the library; the library can be used standalone. Each pipeline stage is a single function in its own module, communicating through plain Python dicts and NetworkX graphs with no shared state and no side effects outside graphify-out/.

nodes.label: Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Each stage is a single function in its own module. They communicate through plain Python dicts and NetworkX graphs with no shared state and no side effects outside graphify-out/.

nodes.label: Leiden algorithm
nodes.rationale: Communities are found using the Leiden algorithm, a graph-clustering method that groups nodes by edge density. No embeddings or vector database needed; semantic similarity edges already in the graph provide the similarity signal.

nodes.label: Three passes
nodes.rationale: graphify processes files in three passes: (1) Code structure extracted locally via tree-sitter with no API calls across 25 languages, (2) Video and audio transcribed locally with faster-whisper seeded with god nodes, (3) Docs, papers, and images processed by Claude subagents which cost tokens.

nodes.label: mcp/sqlite
nodes.rationale: Use mcp/sqlite instead of sqlite-mcp-server because the newer image has a broken entrypoint (/app/.venv/bin/mcp-server-sqlite does not exist in the published layer). mcp/sqlite is marked Archived in catalog metadata but boots and serves correctly.

nodes.label: graphify
nodes.rationale: Designed as an AI coding assistant skill that transforms any folder of files into a knowledge graph. Addresses the raw folder problem. Core design decision: graph structure itself serves as the similarity signal, eliminating the need for a separate embedding step or vector database. Code files are processed locally via tree-sitter AST so file contents never leave the device.

nodes.label: Leiden community detection
nodes.rationale: Clustering is intentionally based on graph topology rather than embeddings. Leiden finds communities through edge density. Semantic similarity edges extracted by Claude are already present in the graph, so they directly influence community detection. The graph structure itself is the similarity signal. No separate embedding step or vector database is needed.

nodes.label: Token benchmark
nodes.rationale: On a mixed corpus of 52 files, queries consume 71.5x fewer tokens compared to reading raw files. The first run performs extraction and graph building, but all subsequent queries read the compact graph instead of the raw corpus, causing savings to compound. SHA256 cache ensures re-runs only reprocess changed files.

nodes.label: Rationale extraction
nodes.rationale: Docstrings, inline comments marked with NOTE, IMPORTANT, HACK, WHY, and design justifications from documents are extracted as rationale_for nodes. This captures not only what code does, but why it was written that way, preserving architectural decision rationale inside the graph.

nodes.label: graphify Pipeline Skill
nodes.rationale: Turn any folder of files into a navigable knowledge graph with community detection, honest audit trail, and three outputs: interactive HTML, GraphRAG-ready JSON, and GRAPH_REPORT.md.

nodes.label: Three-Layer Node Deduplication
nodes.rationale: Node deduplication happens at three layers: within-file AST tracking, between-file via NetworkX add_node idempotency, and semantic merge via explicit seen set before graph construction.

nodes.label: Adaptive Retry on LLM Truncation
nodes.rationale: When LLM returns finish_reason=length, the chunk is split in half and each half re-extracted recursively up to max_retry_depth levels. Signal-driven: dense chunks self-heal by splitting while well-sized chunks pay no extra cost.

nodes.label: SSRF Defense in Depth
nodes.rationale: Multiple layers of SSRF protection: URL scheme validation, private/reserved IP blocking via DNS resolution, DNS rebinding guard via socket patching, redirect re-validation via custom HTTPRedirectHandler, and size capping on response bodies.

nodes.label: Honest Audit Trail
nodes.rationale: Every edge is tagged EXTRACTED, INFERRED, or AMBIGUOUS so users know what was found versus invented. This is a core design principle distinguishing graphify from opaque knowledge graphs.

nodes.label: Three-layer node deduplication strategy
nodes.rationale: Build implements three-layer deduplication: within-file AST dedup, between-file NetworkX overwrite, and semantic merge before build. This ensures stable node identities across extraction passes even when the same entity is found by both AST and LLM extractors.

nodes.label: Cross-community surprise detection
nodes.rationale: Community detection (Leiden/Louvain) finds connections between concepts in different files that users would never think to ask about directly. Surprising connections bridge structurally distant communities.

nodes.label: Honest audit trail via confidence tagging
nodes.rationale: Every edge is tagged EXTRACTED, INFERRED, or AMBIGUOUS so users know what was found in source versus invented by the model. This transparency is central to graphx's trust model.
nodes.norm_label: honest audit trail via confidence tagging

nodes.label: Deterministic Token Fallback for Tests
nodes.rationale: Force the chars/4 fallback so packing math is deterministic regardless of whether tiktoken is installed. tiktoken BPE compresses repeated/synthetic content heavily, which would make pack-size assertions tied to specific input sizes flaky.

nodes.label: ANSI Output Suppression for Windows Compatibility
nodes.rationale: graspologic leiden() can emit ANSI escape sequences that break PowerShell 5.1 scroll buffer on Windows (issue #19). The output suppression in _partition() should prevent any output from leaking.
nodes.norm_label: ansi output suppression for windows compatibility

nodes.label: Adaptive Retry on LLM Output Truncation
nodes.rationale: When LLM output is truncated (finish_reason=length), the system splits the chunk in half and retries recursively, bounded by max_depth to prevent infinite loops.
nodes.norm_label: adaptive retry on llm output truncation

nodes.label: Frontmatter-Aware Content Hashing
nodes.rationale: Cache hashes for .md files ignore frontmatter-only changes but detect body content changes, avoiding unnecessary re-extraction when metadata changes.

nodes.label: Cross-File Call Deduplication
nodes.rationale: Unqualified cross-file calls must not guess between duplicate helper names across files; ambiguous targets should skip the edge rather than create false positives.

nodes.label: Paper Signal Detection in Markdown
nodes.rationale: A .md file with enough paper signals (Abstract, citations, ArXiv references, equations) should classify as PAPER rather than DOCUMENT.

nodes.label: End-to-End Pipeline Validation
nodes.rationale: The full pipeline detect->extract->build->cluster->analyze->report->export runs without LLM calls, using only AST extraction, to catch regressions in module interconnections.

nodes.label: find_cross_references
nodes.rationale: Cross-reference detection is intentionally naive. Keyword overlap of three is a reasonable threshold for short documents but will produce too many false positives on long ones. A real system would use TF-IDF or embedding similarity instead.

nodes.label: save_parsed
nodes.rationale: Storage is intentionally simple. A flat JSON index plus one file per document is enough at small scale. If the corpus grows past a few thousand documents this becomes the bottleneck and should be replaced with SQLite or a proper document store.

nodes.label: Document Pipeline Architecture
nodes.rationale: The pipeline is intentionally linear. Each stage has one job and calls the next stage explicitly. There is no event bus or dependency injection. This makes the call graph easy to follow and easy to test.

nodes.label: Research Notes
nodes.rationale: Open questions include: Should validation happen in the parser or as a separate step? Should cross-references be stored on the document or computed at query time? Is the storage interface the right abstraction?

nodes.label: Graphify Evaluation - httpx Corpus
nodes.rationale: The AST extractor captures structure but not semantics. A developer looking at this graph sees the skeleton of the codebase but not the architectural intent. Adding even a small number of INFERRED edges would significantly improve usefulness.

nodes.label: build_graph
nodes.rationale: Preserves original edge direction as _src/_tgt attributes so display functions show correct direction on undirected graphs.
